revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Catering Order
revealWordProblem.text: Chef Kowalski's pancake batter recipe uses a ratio of 2 cups flour to 3 cups milk. For a big catering order, she uses 14 cups of flour and wants to keep the same ratio. How many cups of milk does she need? Show your scale factor and explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The original ratio is 2 cups flour to 3 cups milk. Kowalski used 14 cups of flour, so the scale factor is 14 ÷ 2 = 7. Multiply the milk amount by the same scale factor: 3 x 7 = 21. She needs 21 cups of milk, since 14:21 simplifies back to 2:3 (14 ÷ 7 = 2 and 21 ÷ 7 = 3), so the ratio stays equivalent.

vocabulary.definition: Decide which ratio is greater, less, or equal by using equivalent ratios or unit rates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Decidir cuál razón es mayor, menor o igual usando razones equivalentes o tasas unitarias.
vocabulary.cloze: Make the ___ match, or find each ___ ___, before deciding which ratio is greater.

examples.why: Both reduced to the same unit.
Different quantities, so the totals say nothing.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate that tells the amount for exactly one unit, like 5 miles per 1 hour, is a ___.

examples.why: The amount for exactly one unit.
A rate for three, not one.

vocabulary.definition: Two ratios that mean the same thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos razones que significan lo mismo.
vocabulary.cloze: Two ratios that make the same comparison are ___ ___.

examples.why: Both parts doubled.
Only one part changed.

vocabulary.definition: To look at ratios and see which is bigger, smaller, or equal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar razones para ver cuál es mayor, menor o igual.
vocabulary.visual: 3:4 vs. 2:5 — which has more of the first ingredient per unit?
vocabulary.cloze: To decide which ratio is greater or if they are equal is to ___ them.

examples.why: It judges one against the other.
Nothing was decided.

vocabulary.definition: To write a ratio with smaller numbers that still compares the same way. 6:8 and 3:4 are the same ratio.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una razón con números más pequeños que compara igual. 6:8 y 3:4 son la misma razón.
vocabulary.cloze: Writing a ratio with smaller numbers that compares the same way, like 6:9 = 2:3, is to ___ it.

examples.why: Both parts divided by 6.
Only one part was divided.

vocabulary.definition: A bottom number that two fractions can share so you can compare them.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número de abajo que dos fracciones pueden compartir para compararlas.
vocabulary.visual: To compare 3/5 and 4/7, use LCD 35: 21/35 vs 20/35
vocabulary.cloze: A denominator shared by two fractions so they can be compared is a ___.

examples.why: One shared bottom number.
Different wholes make the tops meaningless.

vocabulary.term: Convert Measurements within the Same System
vocabulary.termEs: Convertir medidas dentro del mismo sistema
vocabulary.definition: Rewriting a measurement in a different unit of the SAME system, such as feet into inches or liters into milliliters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una medida en otra unidad del MISMO sistema, como pies a pulgadas o litros a mililitros.
vocabulary.cloze: Feet into inches stays inside the ___ measurement system.

examples.why: Both are customary units of capacity.
That crosses into the metric system.

vocabulary.definition: The ratio that links two units in the same measurement system, such as 12 inches to 1 foot. Within one system it is exact.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La razón que relaciona dos unidades del mismo sistema de medición, como 12 pulgadas a 1 pie. Dentro de un mismo sistema es exacta.
vocabulary.cloze: The ratio that trades one unit for another is a ___ ___.

examples.why: It is the fixed ratio that trades one unit for another.
That is the amount being converted, not the factor.

vocabulary.definition: Rewriting a customary measurement as a metric one, or the reverse, so two amounts can be compared.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una medida usual como métrica, o al revés, para poder comparar dos cantidades.
vocabulary.cloze: Rewriting a customary measurement as a metric one gives an ___ answer, not an exact one.

examples.why: Across systems, so approximate.
The factor is rounded; = claims too much.

vocabulary.definition: Ratios that compare quantities in the same relationship.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Razones que comparan cantidades en la misma relación.
vocabulary.visual: 2:3 = 4:6 because both parts were multiplied by 2.
vocabulary.cloze: Ratios that compare quantities in the same relationship are ___ ___.

examples.why: Both parts scaled by the same factor.
Only one part changed.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of two quantities is a ___.

examples.why: Two quantities compared.
Nothing to compare it against.

vocabulary.definition: Use equivalent ratios, tables, graphs, or unit rates to solve a problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar razones equivalentes, tablas, gráficas o tasas unitarias para resolver un problema.
vocabulary.visual: If 3 notebooks cost $6, then 5 notebooks cost $10.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence saying two ratios are equal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática que dice que dos razones son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: An equation that states two ratios are equal is a ___.

examples.why: Two equal ratios stated as one sentence.
Adding ratios is not a proportion.

vocabulary.termEs: Resolución de problemas de razones y tasas
vocabulary.definition: Use ratios and rates to compare quantities and solve real-world problems.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar razones y tasas para comparar cantidades y resolver problemas del mundo real.
vocabulary.visual: Cost = number of items × cost per item.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio comparing two quantities with different units is a ___.

examples.why: Two different units compared.
A single measurement, not a comparison.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying across two ratios to check if they are equal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar en cruz dos razones para ver si son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: Multiplying the numerator of one ratio by the denominator of the other to check a proportion is to ___.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that shows a pattern.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que muestra un patrón.
vocabulary.visual: Cups of juice: 2, 4, 6 | Cups of water: 3, 6, 9
vocabulary.cloze: A table that lists equivalent ratios in rows or columns is a ___.

examples.why: Every column holds the same ratio.
The last column breaks the pattern.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 3.5 · 3.6 · 3.7 · 3.9
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 3.5: Compare ratios fairly by making one part equal or by finding the unit rate. • 3.6: Write the conversion factor as a unit ratio (12 inches : 1 foot), then multiply to go to the smaller unit and divide to go to the larger one. The amount never changes — only the unit does. • 3.7: Write the conversion factor as a ratio (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi), then scale it with a ratio table until it reaches your amount. Between systems the result is approximate, so write ≈, not =. • 3.9: Multiply or divide both numbers by the same amount to make an equivalent ratio.

lines: Lesson 3.5 — Compare Ratio Relationships: Compare ratios fairly by making one part equal or by finding the unit rate.

Lesson 3.6 — Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements within the Same System: Write the conversion factor as a unit ratio (12 inches : 1 foot), then multiply to go to the smaller unit and divide to go to the larger one. The amount never changes — only the unit does.

Lesson 3.7 — Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements Between Systems: Write the conversion factor as a ratio (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi), then scale it with a ratio table until it reaches your amount. Between systems the result is approximate, so write ≈, not =.
Lesson 3.9 — Equivalent Ratios: Multiply or divide both numbers by the same amount to make an equivalent ratio.
linesEs: Lección 3.5 — Comparar relaciones de razón: Compara razones de forma justa igualando una parte o hallando la tasa unitaria.

Lección 3.6 — Razonar con razones: convertir medidas dentro del mismo sistema: Escribe el factor de conversión como una razón unitaria (12 pulgadas : 1 pie), luego multiplica para ir a la unidad más pequeña y divide para ir a la más grande. La cantidad nunca cambia — solo cambia la unidad.

Lección 3.7 — Razonar con razones: convertir medidas entre sistemas: Escribe el factor de conversión como una razón (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi) y luego escálalo con una tabla de razones hasta llegar a tu cantidad. Entre sistemas el resultado es aproximado, así que escribe ≈, no =.
Lección 3.9 — Razones equivalentes: Multiplica o divide los dos números por la misma cantidad para formar una razón equivalente.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Chef Academy's snack bar sells 3 mini quiches for $6 or 5 mini quiches for $8. Which is the better deal per quiche?
optional.explanation: 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche. 5 for $8 is $8 / 5 = $1.60 per quiche. $1.60 < $2.00, so 5 quiches for $8 is the better deal.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche.
The two prices do not reduce to the same cost per quiche. Divide each total by its number of quiches and compare.
Both prices and both counts are given, so a unit price can be calculated for each option.
optional.stemEs: La cafetería de la Academia de Chefs vende 3 mini quiches por $6 o 5 mini quiches por $8. ¿Cuál es la mejor oferta por quiche?
optional.explanationEs: 3 por $6 son $6 / 3 = $2.00 por quiche. 5 por $8 son $8 / 5 = $1.60 por quiche. Como $1.60 < $2.00, 5 quiches por $8 es la mejor oferta.
hints: A better deal means each single quiche costs less, not that the total price is smaller.
Find the unit price for each option: the total cost divided by the number of quiches.
The first option gives $6 ÷ 3 per quiche. Do the same division for $8 and 5 quiches, then compare the two prices.
hintsEs: Una mejor oferta significa que cada quiche cuesta menos, no que el precio total sea menor.
Encuentra el precio por unidad de cada opción: el costo total dividido entre la cantidad de quiches.
La primera opción da $6 ÷ 3 por quiche. Haz la misma división con $8 y 5 quiches y luego compara los dos precios.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.6) How many inches are in 2 feet?
choiceFeedback: That adds 2 + 12.
That subtracts 12 − 2.
12 inches is only 1 foot.
hints: The unit ratio is 12 : 1.
Multiply to reach the smaller unit.
hintsEs: La razón unitaria es 12 : 1.
Multiplica para llegar a la unidad más pequeña.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.7) 1 inch ≈ 2.54 cm. About how many centimeters is 4 inches?
optional.explanation: Scale the conversion factor by 4: 2.54 × 4 = 10.16 centimeters.
choiceFeedback: That adds 4 + 2.54.
That divides, which converts the wrong direction.
hints: The ratio is 1 in : 2.54 cm.
A centimeter is smaller, so the number grows.
optional.stemEs: 1 pulgada ≈ 2.54 cm. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos centímetros son 4 pulgadas?
optional.explanationEs: Escala el factor de conversión por 4: 2.54 × 4 = 10.16 centímetros.
hintsEs: La razón es 1 pulg : 2.54 cm.
Un centímetro es más pequeño, así que el número crece.

optional.stem: (Lesson 3.9) Chef Montoya's dressing uses 3 spoons of oil to 4 spoons of vinegar (3:4). Which recipe card shows an EQUIVALENT ratio?
optional.explanation: Multiply both parts of 3:4 by 3: 3 x 3 = 9 and 4 x 3 = 12, so 9:12 is equivalent to 3:4.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
Only the vinegar was doubled while the oil stayed at 3, so the dressing would taste different. Both parts of a ratio have to be multiplied by the same number.
The same amount was added to each part, and adding does not preserve a ratio — it changes the relationship. Multiply both parts by the same factor instead.
optional.stemEs: El aderezo del chef Montoya usa 3 cucharadas de aceite por 4 cucharadas de vinagre (3:4). ¿Qué tarjeta de receta muestra una razón EQUIVALENTE?
optional.explanationEs: Multiplica ambas partes de 3:4 por 3: 3 × 3 = 9 y 4 × 3 = 12, así que 9:12 es equivalente a 3:4.
hints: Equivalent ratios describe the same relationship, so the dressing tastes the same even when the batch gets bigger.
Pick one multiplier and apply it to both the oil and the vinegar — never to just one of them.
Try tripling the recipe: 3 spoons of oil × 3 gives 9 spoons of oil. Now do the same to the 4 spoons of vinegar and see which card matches.
hintsEs: Las razones equivalentes describen la misma relación, así que el aderezo sabe igual aunque la preparación sea más grande.
Elige un multiplicador y aplícalo tanto al aceite como al vinagre, nunca a uno solo.
Prueba triplicar la receta: 3 cucharadas de aceite × 3 dan 9 cucharadas de aceite. Ahora haz lo mismo con las 4 cucharadas de vinagre y busca la tarjeta que coincida.

optional.instructions: (Lesson 3.5) Find the unit rate for each option to compare them.
hints: Row 1 shows the move: 6 oz for 2 servings became 3 oz per serving by dividing.
Unit rate = ounces ÷ servings. Do that division for Juice B and Juice C, and keep the label 'oz per serving.'
For Juice B, divide 10 ÷ 4 and write the result as ounces per serving. Then repeat with Juice C's numbers.
optional.explanation: A unit rate tells you how many ounces are in exactly 1 serving, so divide ounces by servings. Juice B is 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 oz per serving and Juice C is 9 ÷ 3 = 3 oz per serving. Written per serving, Juice A and Juice C pour the same amount and Juice B pours the least.
optional.explanationEs: Una tasa por unidad te dice cuántas onzas hay en exactamente 1 porción, así que divide las onzas entre las porciones. El Jugo B es 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 oz por porción y el Jugo C es 9 ÷ 3 = 3 oz por porción. Escritos por porción, el Jugo A y el Jugo C sirven la misma cantidad y el Jugo B sirve la menor.
optional.instructionsEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de cada opción para compararlas.
hintsEs: La fila 1 muestra el movimiento: 6 oz para 2 porciones se volvió 3 oz por porción al dividir.
Tasa unitaria = onzas ÷ porciones. Haz esa división para el Jugo B y el Jugo C, y conserva la etiqueta 'oz por porción'.
Para el Jugo B, divide 10 ÷ 4 y escribe el resultado como onzas por porción. Luego repite con los números del Jugo C.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Chef A uses 2 cups of cheese for every 8 crackers. Chef B uses 3 cups of cheese for every 9 crackers. Who uses more cheese per cracker?
approaching.explanation: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 cups per cracker. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 cups per cracker. Chef B uses more cheese per cracker.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Chef A: 2÷8 = ___ cups per cracker.
The two ratios do not reduce to the same value, so they are not equal. Divide each cheese amount by its cracker count and compare the results.
You have both amounts, so a comparison is possible. Turn each ratio into cheese per cracker and the answer appears.
hints: You can't compare 2 cups and 3 cups directly — the chefs use different numbers of crackers.
Find each chef's cheese for ONE cracker: divide cheese by crackers for each, then compare the two rates.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compare those two decimals to see who uses more per cracker.
approaching.stemEs: El chef A usa 2 tazas de queso por cada 8 galletas saladas. El chef B usa 3 tazas de queso por cada 9 galletas saladas. ¿Quién usa más queso por galleta?
approaching.explanationEs: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 tazas por galleta. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 tazas por galleta. El chef B usa más queso por galleta.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 2 tazas y 3 tazas directamente: los chefs usan cantidades distintas de galletas.
Halla el queso de cada chef para UNA galleta: divide queso entre galletas en cada caso y luego compara las dos tasas.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compara esos dos decimales para ver quién usa más por galleta.

approaching.explanation: Convert to the same denominator: 3:4 = 6:8. Since 6:8 > 5:8, the ratio 3:4 is greater.
choiceFeedback: Compare the ratios carefully — which one is greater?
Rewrite both ratios with the same second number before deciding. Scaling 3:4 so its second term is 8 makes the comparison direct.
Both ratios are exact numbers, so they can be compared. Scale one of them until the second terms match.
hints: The second numbers (4 and 8) don't match, so the ratios aren't ready to compare yet.
Rewrite the ratios with the same second number — 8 works nicely, since 4 × 2 = 8 — then compare the first numbers.
Scale 3:4 by 2: multiply both parts to get an out-of-8 ratio. Then compare its first number with the 5 in 5:8.
approaching.explanationEs: Convierte a un denominador común: 3:4 = 6:8. Como 6:8 > 5:8, la razón 3:4 es mayor.
hintsEs: Los segundos números (4 y 8) no coinciden, así que las razones todavía no están listas para compararse.
Reescribe las razones con el mismo segundo número —el 8 funciona bien, porque 4 × 2 = 8— y luego compara los primeros números.
Escala 3:4 por 2: multiplica ambas partes para obtener una razón sobre 8. Luego compara su primer número con el 5 de 5:8.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.6) There are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many inches are in 5 feet?
approaching.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply by the unit ratio: 5 × 12 = 60 inches.
choiceFeedback: That adds 5 + 12. Converting scales the amount, so multiply.
That subtracts 12 − 5. Converting is not a subtraction.
hints: Write the unit ratio first: 12 inches : 1 foot.
Inches are smaller, so the number gets bigger — multiply.
approaching.stemEs: Hay 12 pulgadas en 1 pie. ¿Cuántas pulgadas hay en 5 pies?
approaching.explanationEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que multiplica por la razón unitaria: 5 × 12 = 60 pulgadas.
hintsEs: Escribe primero la razón unitaria: 12 pulgadas : 1 pie.
Las pulgadas son más pequeñas, así que el número se hace mayor — multiplica.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.6) There are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter. How many milliliters are in 3 liters?
approaching.explanation: Multiply by the unit ratio: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 milliliters.
choiceFeedback: That adds instead of multiplying.
30 is far too small — one liter alone is already 1,000 mL.
hints: The unit ratio is 1,000 mL : 1 L.
Milliliters are smaller, so multiply.
approaching.stemEs: Hay 1,000 mililitros en 1 litro. ¿Cuántos mililitros hay en 3 litros?
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplica por la razón unitaria: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 mililitros.
hintsEs: La razón unitaria es 1,000 mL : 1 L.
Los mililitros son más pequeños, así que multiplica.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.7) 1 kilometer ≈ 0.6 mile. About how many miles is 5 kilometers?
approaching.explanation: Scale the conversion factor by 5: 0.6 × 5 = 3 miles.
choiceFeedback: That adds 5 + 0.6 instead of scaling the ratio.
A kilometer is shorter than a mile, so the number of miles must be smaller than 5.
hints: Write the conversion factor as a ratio: 1 : 0.6.
Multiply both parts by 5.
approaching.stemEs: 1 kilómetro ≈ 0.6 millas. ¿Aproximadamente cuántas millas son 5 kilómetros?
approaching.explanationEs: Escala el factor de conversión por 5: 0.6 × 5 = 3 millas.
hintsEs: Escribe el factor de conversión como una razón: 1 : 0.6.
Multiplica las dos partes por 5.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.7) 1 pound ≈ 0.45 kilogram. About how many kilograms is 10 pounds?
choiceFeedback: That adds instead of scaling.
That converts the wrong direction — a kilogram is heavier than a pound.
hints: The ratio is 1 lb : 0.45 kg.
Multiply both parts by 10.
approaching.stemEs: 1 libra ≈ 0.45 kilogramos. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos kilogramos son 10 libras?
hintsEs: La razón es 1 lb : 0.45 kg.
Multiplica las dos partes por 10.

approaching.explanation: Multiply both parts by 2: 2×2 = 4 and 5×2 = 10, so 4:10 is equivalent to 2:5.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
Only the second number was multiplied here — the first part stayed at 2. In equivalent ratios both parts must be multiplied by the same factor.
Those are the right two numbers, but the order got flipped. A ratio compares the first quantity to the second, so the order has to stay the same.
hints: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying BOTH parts of 2:5 by the same number.
For each choice, ask: what did the 2 become, and what did the 5 become? Both must be multiplied by the same amount.
Try multiplying both parts of 2:5 by 2 and see what ratio appears. Then look for that pattern among the choices.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplica ambas partes por 2: 2×2 = 4 y 5×2 = 10, así que 4:10 es equivalente a 2:5.
hintsEs: Las razones equivalentes salen de multiplicar AMBAS partes de 2:5 por el mismo número.
Para cada opción pregunta: ¿en qué se convirtió el 2 y en qué se convirtió el 5? Ambos deben multiplicarse por la misma cantidad.
Prueba multiplicar ambas partes de 2:5 por 2 y mira qué razón aparece. Luego busca ese patrón entre las opciones.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 3.9) A recipe uses 4 eggs for every 6 cups of flour. Which ratio is equivalent?
approaching.explanation: Divide both by 2: 4÷2 = 2 and 6÷2 = 3. The ratio 2:3 is equivalent to 4:6.
choiceFeedback: Scale both numbers by the same factor to make an equivalent ratio.
The flour amount was divided but the eggs stayed the same. Divide both parts of the ratio by the same number to keep it equivalent.
These are the original numbers with the order swapped. Keep eggs first and flour second, then scale both parts the same way.
hints: You can scale a ratio DOWN too — divide both parts by the same number.
Look for a number that divides evenly into both 4 and 6, then divide each part by it.
Both 4 and 6 are even, so divide each by 2 and see what simpler ratio you get.
approaching.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 huevos por cada 6 tazas de harina. ¿Qué razón es equivalente?
approaching.explanationEs: Divide ambas partes entre 2: 4÷2 = 2 y 6÷2 = 3. La razón 2:3 es equivalente a 4:6.
hintsEs: También puedes escalar una razón HACIA ABAJO: divide ambas partes entre el mismo número.
Busca un número que divida exacto tanto al 4 como al 6 y luego divide cada parte entre él.
Tanto 4 como 6 son pares, así que divide cada uno entre 2 y mira qué razón más simple obtienes.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Store A sells 3 mangoes for $6. Store B sells 5 mangoes for $9. Which store offers a better price per mango?
onLevel.explanation: Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango. Store B: $9÷5 = $1.80 per mango. Store B has the better (lower) price per mango.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango.
$6 for 3 and $9 for 5 do not give the same unit price. Divide each total by its number of mangoes to check.
Both the prices and the counts are known, so a unit price can be found for each store.
hints: The stores sell different counts for different prices — compare the price of ONE mango.
Divide dollars by mangoes for each store, then choose the store with the lower per-mango price.
Store A: divide 6 ÷ 3 for its price per mango. Store B: divide 9 ÷ 5. Compare the two prices.
onLevel.stemEs: La tienda A vende 3 mangos por $6. La tienda B vende 5 mangos por $9. ¿Cuál tienda ofrece mejor precio por mango?

Divide dólares entre mangos en cada tienda y luego elige la tienda con el menor precio por mango.
Tienda A: divide 6 ÷ 3 para su precio por mango. Tienda B: divide 9 ÷ 5. Compara los dos precios.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.5) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: Compare Chef Reyes's dressing (4 tbsp oil : 6 tbsp vinegar) to Chef Tran's dressing (5 tbsp oil : 8 tbsp vinegar). Which dressing is oilier?
workedExample.workEs: Compara el aderezo del chef Reyes (4 cdas de aceite : 6 cdas de vinagre) con el del chef Tran (5 cdas de aceite : 8 cdas de vinagre). ¿Cuál aderezo tiene más aceite?

workedExample.label: Find a common denominator
workedExample.work: LCD of 6 and 8 is 24.
workedExample.workEs: El mínimo común denominador de 6 y 8 es 24.

workedExample.label: Scale each ratio
workedExample.work: Chef Reyes: 6 × 4 = 24, so oil = 4 × 4 = 16, giving 16:24. Chef Tran: to reach 24 he also multiplies by 4: oil = 5 × 4 = 20, giving 20:24.
workedExample.workEs: Chef Reyes: 6 × 4 = 24, así que aceite = 4 × 4 = 16, lo que da 16:24. Chef Tran: para llegar a 24 también multiplica por 4: aceite = 5 × 4 = 20, lo que da 20:24.

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: Since 20 > 16, Chef Tran's dressing is oilier.
workedExample.workEs: Como 20 > 16, el aderezo del chef Tran tiene más aceite.

onLevel.correctWork: Each ratio needs its own multiplier to reach 24 — Chef Reyes and Chef Tran do not use the same multiplier. Chef Tran's vinegar is 8, and 8 × 3 = 24 (not 8 × 4 = 32), so multiply BOTH parts of his ratio by 3, not 4: oil = 5 × 3 = 15, giving 15:24. Now compare with equal vinegar (24): Chef Reyes has 16 tbsp oil and Chef Tran has 15 tbsp oil. Since 16 > 15, Chef Reyes's dressing is actually oilier.
hints: Look at Step 3. Each ratio needs its own multiplier to reach the common denominator (24) — Chef Reyes and Chef Tran do not need the same multiplier.
8 × 3 = 24, so what should you multiply BOTH parts of Chef Tran's ratio by?
onLevel.explanation: Each ratio needs its own multiplier to reach 24. Chef Reyes's vinegar 6 × 4 = 24 is right, but Chef Tran's vinegar is 8, and 8 × 3 = 24, so both parts of his ratio scale by 3: 5 × 3 = 15, giving 15:24 instead of 20:24. Compared at equal vinegar, 16 tbsp of oil beats 15, so Chef Reyes's dressing is the oilier one.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada razón necesita su propio multiplicador para llegar a 24. El vinagre del chef Reyes, 6 × 4 = 24, está bien, pero el vinagre del chef Tran es 8, y 8 × 3 = 24, así que las dos partes de su razón se multiplican por 3: 5 × 3 = 15, lo que da 15:24 en vez de 20:24. Comparados con el mismo vinagre, 16 cucharadas de aceite superan a 15, así que el aderezo del chef Reyes es el más aceitoso.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Cada razón necesita su propio multiplicador para llegar a 24 — el chef Reyes y el chef Tran no usan el mismo. El vinagre del chef Tran es 8, y 8 × 3 = 24 (no 8 × 4 = 32), así que multiplica AMBAS partes de su razón por 3, no por 4: aceite = 5 × 3 = 15, lo que da 15:24. Ahora compara con vinagre igual (24): el chef Reyes tiene 16 cdas de aceite y el chef Tran tiene 15 cdas. Como 16 > 15, el aderezo del chef Reyes en realidad tiene más aceite.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. Cada razón necesita su propio multiplicador para llegar al denominador común (24) — el chef Reyes y el chef Tran no necesitan el mismo multiplicador.
8 × 3 = 24, así que ¿por cuánto debes multiplicar AMBAS partes de la razón del chef Tran?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.6) Diamond needs 4 liters of water. Her bottle holds 500 milliliters. How many times must she fill it?

4 liters is 4,000 milliliters.
What times 500 equals 4,000?
onLevel.stemEs: Diamond necesita 4 litros de agua. Su botella contiene 500 mililitros. ¿Cuántas veces debe llenarla?

4 litros son 4,000 mililitros.
¿Qué número por 500 es igual a 4,000?

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.6) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: A recipe needs 2 pounds of flour. The scale reads in ounces (16 oz = 1 lb).
workedExample.workEs: Una receta necesita 2 libras de harina. La balanza marca en onzas (16 oz = 1 lb).

workedExample.label: Step 1
workedExample.work: The unit ratio is 16 ounces : 1 pound.
workedExample.workEs: La razón unitaria es 16 onzas : 1 libra.

workedExample.label: Step 2
workedExample.work: 2 × 16 = 32, so 2 pounds = 32 ounces.
workedExample.workEs: 2 × 16 = 32, así que 2 libras = 32 onzas.

workedExample.label: Step 3
workedExample.work: The scale reads 40 ounces, so there is not enough flour.
workedExample.workEs: La balanza marca 40 onzas, así que no hay suficiente harina.

onLevel.correctWork: Step 3 compares correctly but concludes backwards. The recipe needs 32 ounces and the scale shows 40 ounces. Since 40 > 32, there is MORE than enough flour — 8 ounces extra.
onLevel.explanation: Converting is only half the job. After both amounts share a unit, read the comparison in the direction the question actually asks.
hints: Steps 1 and 2 are correct — check the comparison.
Which is larger, 40 ounces or 32 ounces?
Does more on the scale mean not enough?
onLevel.explanationEs: Convertir es solo la mitad del trabajo. Después de que las dos cantidades compartan una unidad, lee la comparación en la dirección que la pregunta realmente pide.
hintsEs: Los Pasos 1 y 2 son correctos — revisa la comparación.
¿Cuál es mayor, 40 onzas o 32 onzas?
¿Más en la balanza significa que no alcanza?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.7) A dog weighs 31 pounds. Flea medicine comes in packages for 4–10 kg, 10–25 kg, and 25–40 kg. Which package is correct?
onLevel.explanation: 31 pounds ≈ 0.45 × 31 ≈ 14 kilograms, which falls inside the 10–25 kilogram package.
choiceFeedback: 4–10 kg would be about 9–22 pounds, lighter than this dog.
25–40 kg would be about 55–88 pounds, far heavier than this dog.
The ranges are in kilograms — convert the 31 pounds first, and it fits.
hints: The packages are in kilograms but the dog is weighed in pounds.
Convert 31 pounds using 1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg.
About 14 kilograms — which range holds it?
onLevel.stemEs: Un perro pesa 31 libras. El medicamento para pulgas viene en paquetes para 4–10 kg, 10–25 kg y 25–40 kg. ¿Cuál paquete es el correcto?
onLevel.explanationEs: 31 libras ≈ 0.45 × 31 ≈ 14 kilogramos, que cae dentro del paquete de 10–25 kilogramos.
hintsEs: Los paquetes están en kilogramos pero el perro se pesa en libras.
Convierte 31 libras usando 1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg.
Aproximadamente 14 kilogramos — ¿cuál rango lo contiene?
choicesEs: Ninguno — 31 está por encima de todos los rangos

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.7) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: A recipe calls for 2 pounds of flour. The scale is metric. (1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg)
workedExample.workEs: Una receta pide 2 libras de harina. La balanza es métrica. (1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg)

workedExample.label: Step 1
workedExample.work: The conversion factor is 1 : 0.45.
workedExample.workEs: El factor de conversión es 1 : 0.45.

workedExample.label: Step 2
workedExample.work: 0.45 × 2 = 0.9, so 2 pounds ≈ 0.9 kilogram.
workedExample.workEs: 0.45 × 2 = 0.9, así que 2 libras ≈ 0.9 kilogramo.

workedExample.label: Step 3
workedExample.work: 2 pounds = 0.9 kilogram exactly.
workedExample.workEs: 2 libras = 0.9 kilogramo exactamente.

onLevel.correctWork: Step 3 claims an exact equality. The conversion factor 0.45 is rounded (1 pound is about 0.4536 kilogram), so the result must be written 2 pounds ≈ 0.9 kilogram.
onLevel.explanation: Conversions between systems are approximations. Using = instead of ≈ claims a precision the conversion factor never had.
hints: The arithmetic in Step 2 is correct.
Look closely at the symbol used in Step 3.
Is 1 pound exactly 0.45 kilogram?
onLevel.explanationEs: Las conversiones entre sistemas son aproximaciones. Usar = en vez de ≈ afirma una precisión que el factor de conversión nunca tuvo.
hintsEs: La aritmética del Paso 2 es correcta.
Mira con atención el símbolo usado en el Paso 3.
¿1 libra es exactamente 0.45 kilogramos?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 3.9) Marcus earns $45 for every 3 hours of work. How much does he earn in 8 hours?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Unit rate: $45 ÷ 3 = $15/hour.
That is what Marcus would earn for 9 hours, not 8. Find the pay for a single hour first, then multiply by the number of hours the question asks about.
It looks like extra hours were added on top of the original $45 instead of scaling the whole rate. Divide to get the pay for one hour, then multiply by all 8 hours.
hints: 8 hours is not a whole-number multiple of 3 hours, so find what Marcus earns in ONE hour first.
Unit rate: divide the $45 by the 3 hours, then multiply that hourly pay by 8 hours.
Divide 45 ÷ 3 to get dollars per hour — then multiply that rate by 8.
onLevel.stemEs: Marcus gana $45 por cada 3 horas de trabajo. ¿Cuánto gana en 8 horas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: $45 ÷ 3 = $15 por hora. En 8 horas: $15 × 8 = $120.
hintsEs: 8 horas no es un múltiplo entero de 3 horas, así que primero halla cuánto gana Marcus en UNA hora.
Tasa unitaria: divide los $45 entre las 3 horas y luego multiplica ese pago por hora por 8 horas.
Divide 45 ÷ 3 para obtener los dólares por hora y luego multiplica esa tasa por 8.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 3.9) Spot the Common Mistake — Simplifying a Ratio

workedExample.label: Set up the ratio
workedExample.work: A student wants to write 12:18 in simplest form.
workedExample.workEs: Un estudiante quiere escribir 12:18 en su forma más simple.

workedExample.label: Find the common factor
workedExample.work: Both 12 and 18 can be divided by 6.
workedExample.workEs: Tanto 12 como 18 se pueden dividir entre 6.

workedExample.label: Divide each part
workedExample.work: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 3 = 6, so they wrote 2:6.
workedExample.workEs: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 y 18 ÷ 3 = 6, así que escribió 2:6.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: 12:18 simplifies to 2:6
workedExample.workEs: 12:18 se simplifica a 2:6

onLevel.correctWork: Divide BOTH parts by the same number: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so 12:18 simplifies to 2:3.
hints: Look at Step 3. They divided 12 by 6 but divided 18 by 3 — those are different numbers.
To keep ratios equivalent, divide both numbers by the SAME amount. 12:18 divided by 6 each gives 2:3.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error común — Simplificar una razón
onLevel.explanation: The "Divide each part" step uses two different divisors: 12 ÷ 6 but 18 ÷ 3. Simplifying only keeps a ratio equivalent when both parts are divided by the same number, so 12 ÷ 6 = 2 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 give 2:3. The student's 2:6 simplifies to 1:3, which is not the same comparison as 12:18.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Divide each part" usa dos divisores distintos: 12 ÷ 6 pero 18 ÷ 3. Simplificar solo mantiene la razón equivalente cuando ambas partes se dividen entre el mismo número, así que 12 ÷ 6 = 2 y 18 ÷ 6 = 3 dan 2:3. El 2:6 del estudiante se simplifica a 1:3, que no es la misma comparación que 12:18.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Divide AMBAS partes entre el mismo número: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 y 18 ÷ 6 = 3, así que 12:18 se simplifica a 2:3.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. Dividieron 12 entre 6 pero 18 entre 3 — esos son números distintos.
Para mantener razones equivalentes, divide los dos números entre la MISMA cantidad. 12:18 dividido entre 6 cada uno da 2:3.

onLevel.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: (Lesson 3.9) Marcus earns $45 for every 3 hours of work. How much does he earn in 8 hours?
workedExample.workEs: Marcus gana $45 por cada 3 horas de trabajo. ¿Cuánto gana en 8 horas?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió

onLevel.correctWork: The correct answer is $120. Unit rate: $45 ÷ 3 = $15/hour. In 8 hours: $15 × 8 = $120.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es $120. Tasa por unidad: $45 ÷ 3 = $15 por hora. En 8 horas: $15 × 8 = $120.
hints: 8 hours is not a whole-number multiple of 3 hours, so find what Marcus earns in ONE hour first.
hintsEs: 8 horas no es un múltiplo entero de 3 horas, así que primero halla cuánto gana Marcus en UNA hora.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.5) Find Kai's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: Compare 3:5 and 4:7. Which ratio is greater?
workedExample.workEs: Compara 3:5 y 4:7. ¿Cuál razón es mayor?

workedExample.label: Find common denominator
workedExample.work: LCD of 5 and 7 is 35
workedExample.workEs: El mínimo común denominador de 5 y 7 es 35

workedExample.label: Scale the ratios
workedExample.work: 3:5 = 21:35 (3 × 7 = 21). For 4:7, Kai multiplies by 7 again: 4 × 7 = 28, giving 28:35.
workedExample.workEs: 3:5 = 21:35 (3 × 7 = 21). Para 4:7, Kai multiplica por 7 otra vez: 4 × 7 = 28, lo que da 28:35.

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: Since 28 > 21, the ratio 4:7 is greater.
workedExample.workEs: Como 28 > 21, la razón 4:7 es mayor.

extending.correctWork: To scale 4:7 to 35ths, multiply by 35 ÷ 7 = 5, not by 7 again: 4 × 5 = 20, so 4:7 = 20:35 (not 28:35). Now compare correctly: 21:35 vs. 20:35. Since 21 > 20, the ratio 3:5 is actually greater, not 4:7.
hints: Look at Step 3. To turn 7 into 35, Kai should multiply by 35 ÷ 7 = 5 — but he used 7 again, the denominator from the OTHER ratio.
Find the correct multiplier for 4:7 (35 ÷ 7), then multiply BOTH the 4 and the 7 by that number.
extending.explanation: Kai reused the multiplier 7 that belonged to the first ratio instead of finding the one 4:7 actually needs. To reach 35ths you multiply by 35 ÷ 7 = 5, so 4:7 = 20:35, not 28:35. Comparing 21:35 with 20:35 shows 3:5 is the greater ratio — the opposite of the conclusion.
extending.explanationEs: Kai reutilizó el multiplicador 7, que pertenecía a la primera razón, en vez de buscar el que realmente necesita 4:7. Para llegar a treinta y cincoavos se multiplica por 35 ÷ 7 = 5, así que 4:7 = 20:35, no 28:35. Al comparar 21:35 con 20:35 se ve que 3:5 es la razón mayor, lo contrario de la conclusión.
extending.correctWorkEs: Para escalar 4:7 a 35avos, multiplica por 35 ÷ 7 = 5, no por 7 otra vez: 4 × 5 = 20, así que 4:7 = 20:35 (no 28:35). Ahora compara bien: 21:35 vs. 20:35. Como 21 > 20, la razón 3:5 es en realidad la mayor, no 4:7.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. Para convertir 7 en 35, Kai debía multiplicar por 35 ÷ 7 = 5 — pero usó otra vez el 7, el denominador de la OTRA razón.
Halla el multiplicador correcto para 4:7 (35 ÷ 7), luego multiplica TANTO el 4 como el 7 por ese número.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.6) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: Convert 4 liters to milliliters, then find how many 250-mL cups it fills.
workedExample.workEs: Convertir 4 litros a mililitros y hallar cuántos vasos de 250 mL llena.

workedExample.label: Step 3
workedExample.work: It fills 1,000,000 cups.
workedExample.workEs: Llena 1,000,000 de vasos.

extending.correctWork: Step 2 multiplies when it should divide. The question asks how many 250-mL cups fit inside 4,000 mL, which is a division: 4,000 ÷ 250 = 16 cups.
extending.explanation: Converting the units and then splitting the amount into equal parts are two different operations. Converting scaled the unit; sharing 4,000 mL into 250-mL cups is division.
hints: Step 1 is correct. Look at what Step 2 asks for.
How many groups of 250 fit into 4,000?
extending.explanationEs: Convertir las unidades y luego repartir la cantidad en partes iguales son dos operaciones distintas. Convertir cambió la escala de la unidad; repartir 4,000 mL en vasos de 250 mL es una división.
hintsEs: El Paso 1 es correcto. Mira lo que pide el Paso 2.
¿Cuántos grupos de 250 caben en 4,000?

extending.title: (Lesson 3.7) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: Which is longer, 5 kilometers or 5 miles? (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi)
workedExample.workEs: ¿Cuál es más largo, 5 kilómetros o 5 millas? (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi)

workedExample.label: Step 1
workedExample.work: Both numbers are 5.
workedExample.workEs: Los dos números son 5.

workedExample.label: Step 2
workedExample.work: The units are different, so I compare the numbers: they are equal.
workedExample.workEs: Las unidades son distintas, así que comparo los números: son iguales.

workedExample.label: Step 3
workedExample.work: 5 kilometers is the same distance as 5 miles.
workedExample.workEs: 5 kilómetros es la misma distancia que 5 millas.

extending.correctWork: Step 2 compares numbers that are measured in different units. Convert first: 5 kilometers ≈ 0.6 × 5 = 3 miles. Comparing 3 miles with 5 miles shows that 5 miles is the longer distance.
extending.explanation: Equal numbers do not mean equal amounts when the units differ. The whole purpose of a conversion is to make the two amounts comparable before judging them.
hints: What is different about the two measurements besides the number?
Convert one of them so both use the same unit.
extending.explanationEs: Números iguales no significan cantidades iguales cuando las unidades son distintas. El propósito de una conversión es hacer comparables las dos cantidades antes de juzgarlas.
hintsEs: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre las dos medidas además del número?
Convierte una de ellas para que ambas usen la misma unidad.

extending.title: (Lesson 3.9) Find Marcus's Mistake

workedExample.label: Set up the ratio
workedExample.work: 3 cups : 5 cups = ? : 20 cups
workedExample.workEs: 3 tazas : 5 tazas = ? : 20 tazas

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: 7 cups : 20 cups
workedExample.workEs: 7 tazas : 20 tazas

hints: Look at Step 3. What operation should you use with the multiplier?
To keep ratios equivalent, you multiply both parts by the same number — not add.
extending.explanation: In the "Apply to both parts" step Marcus adds the multiplier instead of multiplying by it. Since 5 became 20, the scale factor is × 4, so the first part must be 3 × 4 = 12, giving 12 cups : 20 cups. His 7:20 does not simplify to 3:5, which confirms the ratios are not equivalent.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso "Apply to both parts" Marcus suma el multiplicador en lugar de multiplicar por él. Como 5 pasó a 20, el factor de escala es × 4, así que la primera parte debe ser 3 × 4 = 12, lo que da 12 tazas : 20 tazas. Su 7:20 no se simplifica a 3:5, lo que confirma que las razones no son equivalentes.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. ¿Qué operación debes usar con el multiplicador?
Para mantener razones equivalentes, multiplicas las dos partes por el mismo número — no sumas.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Equivalent Ratios is ADDING the scale factor to one part instead of MULTIPLYING both parts by it. For example, scaling 2:5 by a factor of 4 should give 8:20 (2×4 and 5×4) — not 6:9 (2+4 and 5+4). Adding changes the taste of the recipe (and the value of the ratio); only multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same amount keeps it equivalent.

diagram.title: Scaling the Berry Blast Ratio
diagram.caption: Each row is 5 equal parts: strawberries in 2s and yogurt in 3s. Multiplying both by the scale factor 5 turns 2:3 into 10:15, an equivalent ratio.

connect.scenario: A local smoothie shop sells a Berry Blast smoothie. The recipe calls for 2 cups of strawberries for every 3 cups of yogurt. Today they need to make 15 cups of yogurt worth of smoothies for a catering order.
connect.prompt: Find the scale factor (15 ÷ 3) and use it to figure out how many cups of strawberries the shop needs. Show your steps and explain why multiplying both ingredients by the same factor keeps the smoothie tasting the same.

check.stem: What is the scale factor from 3 cups of yogurt to 15 cups?
check.explanation: 15 ÷ 3 = 5. The recipe is being made 5 times over.

check.stem: How many cups of strawberries are needed?
check.explanation: Multiply the strawberries by the same factor: 2 × 5 = 10 cups.

check.stem: Why must both ingredients be multiplied by the same factor?
choices: So the ratio stays 2:3 and the smoothie tastes the same
Because 2 and 3 are both small numbers
So the total is a whole number
check.explanation: An equivalent ratio comes from scaling both parts equally. 10:15 simplifies back to 2:3; changing only one part would change the flavor.

connect.modelAnswer: The scale factor is 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so the shop needs 2 × 5 = 10 cups of strawberries with the 15 cups of yogurt. Multiplying both parts by 5 keeps the ratio 10:15 = 2:3, so the smoothie tastes exactly the same.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 3.6) There are 4 cups in 1 quart. A soup recipe calls for 5 quarts of broth. How many cups is that, and why?
choices: 20 cups, because cups are smaller so I multiply: 5 × 4
5 cups, because the amount does not change
exitTicket.explanation: The unit ratio is 4 cups : 1 quart. A cup is smaller than a quart, so it takes more of them: 5 × 4 = 20 cups.
choiceFeedback: Dividing converts to the LARGER unit. Cups are smaller than quarts, so the number must grow.
Converting scales the amount by the unit ratio; it is never an addition.
The amount of broth does not change, but the NUMBER does, because the unit changed.
hints: Write the unit ratio first: 4 cups to 1 quart.
Is a cup smaller or larger than a quart? Smaller units take a bigger number.
exitTicket.stemEs: (Repaso rápido, de la lección 3.6) Hay 4 tazas en 1 cuarto. Una receta de sopa pide 5 cuartos de caldo. ¿Cuántas tazas son y por qué?
choicesEs: 20 tazas, porque las tazas son más pequeñas así que multiplico: 5 × 4
5 tazas, porque la cantidad no cambia
exitTicket.explanationEs: La razón unitaria es 4 tazas : 1 cuarto. Una taza es más pequeña que un cuarto, así que se necesitan más: 5 × 4 = 20 tazas.
choiceFeedbackEs: Dividir convierte a la unidad más grande. Las tazas son más pequeñas que los cuartos, así que el número tiene que crecer.
Convertir escala la cantidad por la razón unitaria; nunca es una suma.
La cantidad de caldo no cambia, pero el número sí, porque la unidad cambió.
hintsEs: Escribe primero la razón unitaria: 4 tazas a 1 cuarto.
¿Una taza es más pequeña o más grande que un cuarto? Las unidades más pequeñas llevan un número más grande.
